data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and reviewing weak units (6 & 7) to solidify concepts before the exam.
data.summary: This 16-week plan prioritizes Units 6 and 7 in the first half to address weaknesses, while systematically covering foundational units 1-5 and 8. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to ensure exam readiness.

weeks.focus: Master rotational energy and momentum concepts.
tasks: Do 10 free-response questions on rotational kinetic energy and torque work, then mark them against the scoring guide.
Solve 5 problems on conservation of angular momentum, focusing on inelastic rotational collisions.

weeks.focus: Understand the fundamentals of simple harmonic motion.
tasks: Derive the period formula for a mass-spring system and a pendulum, then solve 8 practice problems.
Analyze 5 SHM graphs to identify amplitude, period, and phase.
Complete 10 vector addition problems in 2D, including projectile motion components.
Solve 5 relative motion problems using reference frames.

weeks.focus: Apply Newton's laws to complex systems.
tasks: Draw free-body diagrams for 10 systems with friction and tension, then calculate acceleration.
Solve 5 problems involving Newton's Third Law action-reaction pairs.
Solve 10 problems using conservation of mechanical energy, including springs and gravity.
Calculate power in 5 scenarios involving constant force and velocity.
Do 8 impulse-momentum theorem problems, then 5 collision problems (elastic and inelastic).
Solve 3 multi-step problems combining momentum and energy conservation.
Solve 10 torque problems, including static equilibrium and rotational acceleration.
Calculate rotational inertia for 5 different shapes and apply it to Newton's Second Law for rotation.
Redo 5 difficult problems from Week 1 on angular momentum conservation.
Solve 3 mixed problems involving both linear and rotational kinetic energy.
Solve 8 problems on energy exchange in SHM systems, including phase shifts.
Analyze 5 experimental setups to determine spring constants and periods.
Solve 10 problems on pressure, density, and buoyancy.
Apply Bernoulli's equation to 5 fluid flow scenarios.
Do 10 mixed problems combining projectile motion with force analysis.
Solve 5 problems involving circular motion and centripetal force.
Solve 8 problems combining work-energy theorem with impulse-momentum.
Do 5 collision problems where energy is not conserved but momentum is.
Solve 5 problems combining torque with fluid pressure.
Redo 3 difficult SHM problems from Week 9.
Complete a 45-minute timed set of 10 questions on Units 6 and 7.
Review errors and redo 5 incorrect problems with detailed explanations.
Take a full 3-hour AP Physics 1 practice exam (multiple choice and free response).
Score the exam and identify weak areas for final review.
Review all incorrect answers from the practice exam in Week 15.
Do 5 quick review problems on each unit to maintain familiarity.
